title: US and UK Regulators Intensify AI Probes to Block Systemic Risks
summary:
The Federal Reserve, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) are questioning banks about the deployment of agentic AI and models developed in China. These US watchdogs are focusing on whether autonomous cyberdefense agents can be monitored, audited, and shut down to prevent rogue systems from destabilizing the financial sector.

UK authorities are also requiring large banks to review independent backup systems to ensure continuity if primary infrastructure is compromised. The expanded oversight follows warnings from a senior European bank executive that AI could cause severe damage to banking markets within 6 months, with regulators fearing that automated attacks could undermine global systemic stability.

The Fed, OCC and FDIC are questioning banks about Chinese-developed AI models and whether autonomous cyberdefense agents can be monitored, audited and shut down.

And UK regulators are asking major banks to examine fully independent backup systems in case their primary infrastructure is compromised.
